question.prompt: Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is inscribed in circle \(O\) and has sides \(AB=3,\) \(BC=2,\) \(CD=6,\) and \(DA=8.\) Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be points on \(BD\) such that \(\dfrac{DX}{BD}=\dfrac{1}{4}\) and \(\dfrac{BY}{BD}=\dfrac{11}{36}.\) Let \(E\) be the intersection of line \(AX\) and the line through \(Y\) parallel to \(AD.\) Let \(F\) be the intersection of line \(CX\) and the line through \(E\) parallel to \(AC.\) Let \(G\) be the point on circle \(O\) other than \(C\) that lies on line \(CX.\) What is \(XF\cdot XG?\)

solutions.title: Similarity, chord products, and the diagonal
solutions.explanation:
The parallel lines create similar triangles that let us transfer the desired product to segments on \(BD\).

Let \(d=BD\). Since \(DX=d/4\), we have \(BX=3d/4\). Also \(BY=11d/36\), so the points occur in the order \(B,Y,X,D\), and
\[
XY=BX-BY=\left(\frac34-\frac{11}{36}\right)d=\frac49d.
\]
Because \(YE\parallel AD\) and \(EF\parallel AC\), respectively,
\[
\triangle XEY\sim\triangle XAD,
\qquad
\triangle XEF\sim\triangle XAC.
\]
Their corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{XY}{XD}=\frac{XE}{XA}=\frac{XF}{XC}.
\]
The intersecting chords \(BD\) and \(CG\) pass through \(X\). By power of a point,
\[
XC\cdot XG=XB\cdot XD.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
XF\cdot XG
&=\frac{XY}{XD}(XC\cdot XG)\\
&=XB\cdot XY
=\left(\frac34d\right)\left(\frac49d\right)
=\frac{d^2}{3}.
\end{aligned}
\]
It remains to find \(d^2\). Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary. Thus, if \(\alpha=\angle BAD\), then \(\angle BCD=180^\circ-\alpha\), whose cosine is \(-\cos\alpha\). Apply the law of cosines in triangles \(ABD\) and \(BCD\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
d^2&=3^2+8^2-2(3)(8)\cos\alpha
=73-48\cos\alpha,\\
d^2&=2^2+6^2-2(2)(6)\cos(180^\circ-\alpha)
=40+24\cos\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
Adding the first equation to twice the second cancels the cosine terms:
\[
3d^2=73+2(40)=153,
\qquad d^2=51.
\]
Therefore
\[
XF\cdot XG=\frac{51}{3}=\boxed{17},
\]
which is choice A.
